nodes.summary: Because the parent validation curve peaks and then declines while training continues, indicating overfit, a factorial cross-stage search over FM versus DCN-lite, logloss versus 0.5-BPR hybrid, uniform versus 7-day recency weighting, and mild versus strong regularization will identify an interaction that improves validation primary by approximately 0.0029. [grey-zone confirm failed (mean delta +0.0006)]

selection.citation: factorial experiment design (Fisher; standard DOE practice); ablation-study methodology.
selection.why: Validation peaks at epoch 8 and then declines while training loss continues downward, indicating overfit. A cross-stage matrix directly addresses the prior run's attribution failure by testing architecture, loss, recency weighting, and regularization combinations under comparable probes. It preserves the required capacity-plus-regularization interaction, adds half-epoch checkpointing, and has an honest best-known target near 0.6047, about +0.0029 over the 0.6018 baseline—large enough to clear epsilon.

rejected.reason: Promising, but it repeats the previously tried compound opening and tunes its dials without first resolving which bundled stages actually contributed.
It matches the overfit curve, but its standalone measured gain is about +0.0015, below the +0.002 convergence threshold.
Premature on a baseline parent, and a prior three-seed ensemble was already rejected; individual competitive configurations should be established first.

nodes.summary: Because validation primary peaks around epoch 8 and then declines, indicating overfit to older training behavior under temporal shift, normalized 7-day exponential recency weighting alone will improve validation primary by approximately 0.0015 relative to the parent FM.

selection.citation: standard temporal covariate-shift weighting; KuaiRand date-split research notes
selection.why: Validation peaks at epoch 8 and declines through epoch 10 while training loss generally falls, diagnosing overfit. However, overfit and underfit families are portfolio-excluded, and recency-weighting is the eligible active data-shift method. The temporal next-week split makes recent behavior more predictive than stale rows. Expected gain is honestly only about +0.001 on average, so this is exploratory rather than likely to clear epsilon; normalize weights, preserve effective sample size, checkpoint early, and confirm across seeds.

rejected.reason: It directly fits the overfit curve and is well evidenced, but the overfit family is explicitly excluded by portfolio diversity.
Its overfit and underfit treatment families are excluded, and the prior rejected node already attempted a closely related cross-stage package search.
Although temporal context is plausible, its flat-signal family intersects the excluded portfolio and its incremental gain is uncertain.

nodes.summary: Because the parent validation score peaks and then falls while training loss continues improving, indicating overfit, a two-stage joint dial search over the literature-backed DCN-lite, 0.5-BPR hybrid, dropout/AdamW step-decay regularization, and recency-weighting package will improve validation primary by approximately 0.0029. (delta +0.0024)

selection.citation: standard hyperparameter search practice (random/grid search, Bergstra & Bengio JMLR 2012); package composition per DCNv2/BPR training setups.
selection.why: Validation peaks at epoch 8 and then declines while training loss continues downward, indicating overfit. With two convergence strikes already spent, isolated regularization or recency changes have an honest expected gain below the 0.002 reset threshold. This untried card is the strongest available single-node option: it tunes the literature-backed DCN-lite, hybrid-loss, strong-regularization, and recency package jointly, then uses half-epoch checkpoint selection. The same package has replicated near 0.6047, implying roughly +0.0029 over the 0.6018 baseline, while the internal sweep addresses why the earlier shallow cross-stage search reached only 0.6020.

rejected.reason: It directly fits the overfit curve, but its measured standalone gain is about +0.0015, below epsilon and likely to end the run after the current two-strike streak.
A factorial cross-stage search was already attempted in node_001 and failed at 0.6020; repeating that broad opening is less justified than densely tuning the known interacting package.
Recency weighting alone was already rejected at 0.6017 and is known to require a stable regularized ranker.
Ensembling is a closing move for a reproducibly competitive champion; the current accepted champion remains the baseline, and a prior premature ensemble was rejected.

nodes.summary: Adding a validation-selected cumulative ordinal watch-ratio auxiliary loss to the accepted regularized DCN-lite 0.5-BPR hybrid will improve validation primary by at least 0.002 by learning duration-aware engagement structure without using watch-time outcomes at inference.

Because validation peaks early and then declines, indicating residual overfit and seed variance, validation-selecting member count {3,5,7} and probability versus per-user-rank aggregation for independent replicas of the accepted regularized DCN-lite champion will improve validation primary by approximately 0.0008. (delta +0.0013)

selection.citation: Deep Ensembles (Lakshminarayanan et al., NeurIPS 2017); rank aggregation practice.
selection.why: The journal reports validation peaking and then declining, and the accepted regularized package at 0.6042 is already near the benchmark ceiling. With a two-strike convergence streak and only small gains realistically remaining, this is a closing variance-reduction move. Unlike the previously rejected fixed three-seed rank ensemble, this untried card validates member count, probability versus per-user-rank averaging, and modest dial diversity on the accepted champion. Expected gain is honestly only about +0.0004 to +0.0015, unlikely to clear epsilon, but it is the strongest justified final-stage option.

rejected.reason: The ordinal auxiliary already reduced the champion to 0.6030, CWM and ordinal FM forms are measured dead, and recency is already in the accepted package; the remaining combinations have weak evidence and high runtime.

A fixed three-seed rank ensemble was already rejected; the design sweep is materially broader and can diagnose whether aggregation rule, member count, or modest configuration diversity caused that failure.

Although previously replicated on a baseline, it is running elsewhere and its incremental gain on the tuned package is uncertain; at N-1 convergence pressure, a validated closing ensemble design is safer.
